notes:
Lead: Head of ML infra (Ethan Park) running evaluation for critical inference workloads supporting quant research and trade surveillance. Primary ask: dedicated capacity with strict throughput guarantees and predictable latency SLOs. Key fragments from calls:
- "We need tail latency at scale — trading alerts must be sub-50ms 95th for short probes" (paraphrase).
- Want explicit reserved-GPU planning: preliminary ask = capacity equivalent to 8xA100-ish for baseline, with burst pool for spikes. Team asked for cost model: reserved vs burst pricing, overage rules, and ramp schedule.

Technical requirements / priorities:
- Workloads: reranking for post-trade matching (~500 qps peak, 2000 qps on event spikes), embeddings index updates (batch nightly, high throughput), analyst chat summarization (low latency interactive).
- Latency SLOs: 95th <= 50ms for trading lane (short context), 99th <= 200ms for analyst chat, background lanes can be best-effort.
- Throughput guarantees: sustained token throughput target ~1.5M tokens/minute for committed pool; want guarantees on sustained compute (not just burst).
- Reserved GPU planning: preference for Nvidia A100/RTX A6000 equivalent; request SKU mapping and a cost/throughput table. Discussed option for mixed pool (low-precision quantized variants for background).

Traffic shaping & priority lanes specifics (core of evaluation):
- Tenant isolation: absolute requirement for production; per-tenant cgroups or physical partitioning for highest tier. They prefer hard isolation for trading flows, shared pools OK for lower tiers.
- Per-route quotas: must be able to bind quota to API route (eg /v1/generate-trade-alerts) with per-second token and concurrency caps.
- Priority lanes: want two lane model — "fast-lane" (strict SLA, preemption of background work) and "background-lane" (cheap, batched). Fast-lane needs admission control + admission queue length metrics.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: circuit breakers, automatic deprioritization, per-GPU tenant shaping; want eviction / slowdown thresholds and transparent metrics.
- Admission policies: fair-share across teams plus static reservations for market-critical apps; need policy examples.

SLA negotiation topics raised by procurement/legal:
- Uptime and latency credits, scheduled maintenance windows, incident response SLOs. They pushed back on a 99.95% uptime without credit tiers.
- Data handling: retention, ability to purge training logs, KMS keys for model cache encryption.

POC plan agreed:
- Week 0: baseline perf workshop + map workloads to configs (done 2024-09-30).
- Week 1-2: deploy Dedicated eval in LCA VPC, run synthetic traffic for throughput curves (se_assigned: Rafael).
- Week 3: noisy-neighbor test (concurrent heavy embeddings + low-latency lane) to validate priority lanes and preemption semantics.
- Week 4: security review + SLA redline pass with legal + cost model finalize.

Stated budget and constraints: finance prefers multi-yr reserved commit if unit economics hit target; strong cost sensitivity on sustained token cost (want 30-40% improvement vs current internal run).

Quotes / call snippets: "If you can't guarantee the lane semantics, we can't move mission-critical traffic to it." — Ethan Park.

Action items for Redwood team (from meeting 2024-10-21):
- Deliver A100-equivalent sizing table with sustained throughput numbers and cost delta (by 2024-10-25) — Rafael
- Run noisy-neighbor scenario and send results + flamegraphs (by 2024-10-28) — infra-eng POC
- Legal to circulate SLA redline template and proposed credits (Maya to follow)

Summary: High-value enterprise opportunity. Main decision hinge = validated priority-lane behavior under noisy neighbor conditions and acceptable SLA/legal terms. Next major milestone = POC completion and procurement committee decision in Dec.
